sentences.en: In the 3rd century BC, China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, made a bold proclamation.
sentences.zh: 公元前3世纪，中国的第一位皇帝秦始皇发表了一项豪迈的宣言。
他的朝代将延续一万世。

sentences.en: He launched an obsessive quest for immortality.
sentences.zh: 他展开了对长生不老的痴迷追求。

sentences.en: He ordered expeditions to the Eastern Sea, demanded his subject search for an elixir of life,
sentences.zh: 他下令向东海派遣探险队，要求臣民寻找长生不老药，

sentences.en: and even welcomed mystics into his court.
sentences.zh: 甚至欢迎方士来到他的宫廷。

sentences.en: His obsession came at a cost,
putting him at odds with Confucian scholars at the time.
sentences.zh: 使他与当时的儒生产生了对立。

sentences.en: Historians have pieced together parts of Qin Shi Huang's story
sentences.zh: 历史学家们拼凑出了秦始皇故事的一部分，

sentences.en: from thousands of wooden strips unearthed in Hunan province.
sentences.zh: 这些内容来自湖南省出土的数千枚竹简。
这些竹简记录了他的书信往来。

sentences.en: These writings included responses from the emperor's minions,
sentences.zh: 这些文字包括来自皇帝手下的回复，

sentences.en: who were too afraid to tell their boss what they really thought.
sentences.zh: 他们太害怕了，不敢把真实想法告诉老板。

sentences.en: According to the BBC, the notes featured, quote,
sentences.zh: 据BBC报道，这些便条的特色是，引述一段话，

sentences.en: assorted awkward replies from regional governments who had failed to find the key to eternal life.
sentences.zh: 地方政府给出的各种尴尬答复，他们未能找到永生的钥匙。

sentences.en: Qin Shi Huang did achieve extraordinary things during his lifetime.
sentences.zh: 秦始皇在他的一生中确实取得了非凡的成就。

sentences.en: He unified China, standardized currency and measures, built roads and canals,
sentences.zh: 他统一了中国，统一度量衡，修建了道路和运河，

sentences.en: and linked fortresses into what became the Great Wall.
sentences.zh: 并将要塞连成了后来的长城。

sentences.en: But he never found the key to immortality.
sentences.zh: 但他从未找到长生不老的钥匙。

sentences.en: He died in 210 BC at the age of 49.
sentences.zh: 他在公元前210年去世，享年49岁。

sentences.en: Even in death, he refused to believe death was the end.
sentences.zh: 即使在死后，他也拒绝相信死亡就是终点。

sentences.en: His monumental mausoleum, guarded by thousands of terracotta soldiers,
sentences.zh: 他那宏伟的陵墓由数千名兵马俑守卫，

sentences.en: was designed to protect him on his journey into the afterlife.
sentences.zh: 旨在保护他踏上通往来世的旅程。

sentences.en: What could cause such desperation, such obsession, such refusal to face the inevitable?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了这样的绝望、这样的痴迷、这样的拒绝面对不可避免的事实？

sentences.en: And is it possible that all of us share something in common with the great Chinese emperor?
sentences.zh: 我们所有人是否有可能与这位伟大的中国皇帝有某些共同点？

sentences.en: This is the second part of our exploration into how design thinking can help you lead a more meaningful life.
sentences.zh: 这是我们关于设计思维如何帮助你过上更有意义的生活的第二部分探索。

sentences.en: If you missed the first story, you can find it in our podcast feed or at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你错过了第一个故事，你可以在我们的播客源或 hiddenbrain.org 上找到它。

sentences.en: It's the episode titled, Designing a Life That Matters.
sentences.zh: 这就是题为《设计重于泰山的生活》的那集节目。

sentences.en: How we seek to avoid the truth and the costs of not facing reality.
sentences.zh: 我们如何试图逃避真相，以及不面对现实的代价。

sentences.en: There are times of joy, times of sorrow, and times of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 有快乐的时光，有悲伤的时光，也有充满不确定的时光。

sentences.en: Along the way, we inevitably face setbacks, obstacles, and disappointment.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，我们不可避免地会面临挫折、障碍和失望。

sentences.en: At Stanford University, Dave Evans says that one way we cope with these challenges
sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，戴夫·埃文斯说，我们应对这些挑战的一种方式

sentences.en: is by telling ourselves stories, narratives that help us make sense of what's happening to us.
sentences.zh: 就是通过给自己讲故事，用这些叙事来帮助我们理解正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Dave Evans, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 戴夫·埃文斯，欢迎来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Shankar, good to be with you again.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，很高兴再次与你同行。

sentences.en: Dave, you had a friend named Gary.
sentences.zh: 戴夫，你曾有个朋友叫加里。

sentences.en: How did the two of you meet and get to know each other?
sentences.zh: 你们俩是怎么相遇并相识的？

sentences.en: Well, our kids were of similar age, and we frequented the same church.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们的孩子年龄相仿，我们经常去同一座教堂。

sentences.en: We lived in the same town, so we were neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我们住在同一个镇上，所以我们是邻居。

sentences.en: One day, Gary came to you with a problem.
sentences.zh: 有一天，加里带着一个问题来找你。

sentences.en: Tell me what he told you.
sentences.zh: 告诉我他对你说了什么。

sentences.en: Well, his problem was he was having strokes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他的问题是他开始中风了。

sentences.en: And it turned out he came from a long line of people who have strokes.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他的家族有中风的病史。

sentences.en: He was a technical writer in Silicon Valley.
sentences.zh: 他是硅谷的一名技术作家。

sentences.en: And he was having a good career.
sentences.zh: 他的职业生涯发展得很顺利。

sentences.en: And his problem was, how could he get back to working full-time?
sentences.zh: 他的问题是，他该如何恢复全职工作？

sentences.en: He'd had to take a stop out the way his stroke had hit him, was getting in the way of his ability to work.
sentences.zh: 他不得不中途停下来，中风对他的打击方式妨碍了他的工作能力。

sentences.en: And he was wondering if I could help him figure out a way to get his skills back to where he could get back on the job.
sentences.zh: 他想知道我是否能帮他想个办法，把他的技能恢复到能够重返工作岗位的水平。

sentences.en: So his problem was, he said, I have a job that I like.
sentences.zh: 所以他的问题是，他说，我有一份我喜欢的工作。

sentences.en: I'm doing what I want to do, but I have this pesky little thing, which is my body is not allowing me to do what I want to do.
sentences.zh: 我在做我想做的事，但我有这么个讨厌的小毛病，那就是我的身体不允许我做我想做的事。

sentences.en: And I want you to get my body out of the way so I can go back to doing what I want to do.
sentences.zh: 我希望你把我的身体挪开，这样我就可以回去做我想做的事。

sentences.en: He said, well, you know, this, I mean, the problem is, Deb, I, you know, my, my father died of a stroke.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，这个，我的意思是，问题是，戴夫，我，你知道，我的，我父亲死于中风。

sentences.en: My brother died of a stroke in his late 50s.
sentences.zh: 我哥哥在快60岁时死于中风。

sentences.en: He was about 52 at the time or something like that.
He said, so I don't want to be that guy.
sentences.zh: 他说，所以，我不想成为那样的人。

sentences.en: Everything's got to happen for a reason.
So it must be that there's something I'm supposed to learn.
sentences.zh: 所以一定有什么东西是我应该去学习的。

sentences.en: So if I were, if I could learn what it is that this malady has tried to teach me, then maybe it can stop and I can get my life back.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我能，如果我能弄明白这个疾病试图教给我的是什么，那么也许它就会停止，我就可以找回我的生活。

sentences.en: So what I really need to do is figure out why I need to learn something from this and what is it?
sentences.zh: 所以我真正需要做的是弄清楚为什么我需要从中学习一些东西，以及它到底是什么？

sentences.en: Can you help me with that?
I'm wondering how you responded to this request of his to help him understand what his body was trying to tell him,
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是如何回应他的这个请求的，他让你帮他理解他的身体试图告诉他什么，

sentences.en: the message it was trying to give him.
I was stuck a little bit because I thought, oh my God, I don't think that's what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我当时有点卡壳了，因为我想，噢天哪，我觉得事情根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: And here's this guy who's a lovely guy.
sentences.zh: 而这家伙又是个可爱的人。

sentences.en: And, and the truth is he's dying.
sentences.zh: 而且，事实是他在走向死亡。

sentences.en: The truth is he's got a severe medical threat and it's not going well.
sentences.zh: 事实是，他面临着严重的医疗威胁，而且情况很不妙。

sentences.en: And he's counting on me to help him get some place.
sentences.zh: 他指望我能帮他去往某个地方。

sentences.en: I don't think he can go.
So what I was really struggling with is how do I deliver the bad news that Gary,
sentences.zh: 所以我真正纠结的是，我该如何传递这个坏消息：加里，

sentences.en: I think you're asking the wrong question.
I'm wondering whether Gary was getting feedback from other people that was trying to answer the question that he wanted answered,
sentences.zh: 我想知道加里是否从其他人那里得到了反馈，这些人试图回答他想要解答的问题，

sentences.en: even if it wasn't the right question.
sentences.zh: 即使这不是正确的问题。

sentences.en: Well, yes, unfortunately, he was surrounded with well-meaning, cheerful people who wanted him to feel better, you know?
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，不幸的是，他身边围着一些善意、开朗的人，他们希望他感觉好点，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And so there were a group of guys he regularly had lunch with and they were encouraging like,
sentences.zh: 所以有一群经常和他一起吃午饭的人，他们一直在鼓励他，比如，

sentences.en: And he goes, I'm going to try to get back to where they go.
sentences.zh: 而他说，我要努力回到他们去的地方。

sentences.en: You know, so they all were trying to cheerlead.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以他们都在试图加油鼓劲。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, they were cheerleading him down where I thought it was a dead end that was going to end very, very badly.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他们鼓励他走向我认为是一条死胡同的地方，那将以非常非常糟糕的方式收场。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's the old phrase, the road to hell is paved with good intention.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，有句老话，通往地狱的路是用好意铺就的。

sentences.en: There's a lot of good intention surrounding him.
But frankly, I think it was going a terrible place.
sentences.zh: 但坦白说，我认为这正通往一个糟糕的地方。

sentences.en: It must have placed you in a very difficult situation, Dave, because a friend is coming to you with this very serious problem.
sentences.zh: 这一定把你置于一个非常困难的境地，戴夫，因为一个朋友带着这么严重的问题来找你。

sentences.en: You feel like your friend is not looking at reality for what it is.
sentences.zh: 你觉得你的朋友没有正视现实的本来面目。

sentences.en: Other friends are basically encouraging Gary in his delusion.
sentences.zh: 其他朋友基本上都在助长加里的幻想。

sentences.en: Well, keep in mind, I met Gary at church, which means, you know, he was a person of faith.
sentences.zh: 嗯，记住，我是在教堂认识加里的，这意味着，你知道，他是一个有信仰的人。

sentences.en: And that was a big part of the story.
sentences.zh: 那是这个故事的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: And so it wasn't just what's the lesson that my body is trying to teach me, but what is God trying to tell me?
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅是“我的身体试图教给我什么课”，而且是“上帝试图告诉我什么”？

sentences.en: He says, because I'm pretty sure this must be a lesson God is giving me that if I can persevere through and learn the lesson, then I get to get out of jail.
sentences.zh: 他说，因为我很确信这一定上帝给我的一个教训，如果我能坚持过去并学到这个教训，那么我就可以刑满释放了。

sentences.en: You know, and I didn't think that was likely to happen because despite the fact that I do happen to believe in God, God doesn't fix every problem.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得这不太可能发生，因为尽管我的确碰巧相信上帝，但上帝并不会解决每一个问题。

sentences.en: God doesn't instruct himself and miraculously fix everything.
sentences.zh: 上帝不会自我指示并奇迹般地解决一切。

sentences.en: And it's nice to think that's what's coming your way, but you're not in charge of that.
sentences.zh: 认为好事将要降临固然很好，但你并不负责这一切。

sentences.en: You may not be the miracle child.
sentences.zh: 你可能不是那个受奇迹眷顾的孩子。

sentences.en: And so I asked him, point black note, Gary, why is it you believe this?
sentences.zh: 所以我直截了当地问他，加里，为什么你坚信这一点？

sentences.en: And he said, well, what else could it possibly be?
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，除此之外还能是什么呢？

sentences.en: There's got to be a reason for this.
I said, well, let's look at what the other reasons might be.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，让我们看看可能还有什么其他原因。

sentences.en: He said, what do you mean?
I said, well, maybe the reason you're having strokes, Gary, isn't because God is going to use you as the demonstration of a miracle.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，也许你中风的原因，加里，并不是因为上帝要用你来展示一个奇迹。

sentences.en: But maybe you're having strokes because you've got really crappy DNA and brain chemistry that breaks down at about 50 to 55 years old.
sentences.zh: 而是也许你中风是因为你有真的很糟糕的基因和大脑化学机制，它在大约50到55岁时就会崩溃。

sentences.en: Because, you know, we live in a broken world and some of that brokenness falls on everybody.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，我们生活在一个破碎的世界里，其中一些破碎会降临到每个人身上。

sentences.en: We're all going to die, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们终将一死。

sentences.en: All we're talking about is timing.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的全部只是时间问题。

sentences.en: And I told him the story of the head of the gerontology department at Harvard Medical School, who I got stuck on the ground during an ice storm in Chicago with years ago,
sentences.zh: 我给他讲了哈佛医学院老年学系主任的故事，多年前我在芝加哥的一场冰风暴中被困在地面上时遇到了他，

sentences.en: who reminded me almost nobody dies of old age.
sentences.zh: 他提醒我，几乎没有人是死于衰老。

sentences.en: They died of disease or starvation or an accident.
sentences.zh: 他们死于疾病、饥饿或事故。

sentences.en: I said, so, Gary, you're not going to die of old age.
sentences.zh: 我说，所以，加里，你不会老死。

sentences.en: You're going to die of something else, and maybe you're going to die of a stroke.
sentences.zh: 你会死于其他原因，也许你会死于中风。

sentences.en: So maybe what's going on is, how do you live well through being a person who comes from a long line of guys with bad stroke DNA?
sentences.zh: 所以也许现在的情况是，作为一个有着长长糟糕中风DNA家族史的人，你该如何好好生活？

sentences.en: And he just stared at me.
He said, do you think that might be it?
sentences.zh: 他说，你觉得会是这样吗？

sentences.en: I said, well, Gary, lots of people die in their 50s.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，加里，很多人在50多岁时去世。

sentences.en: You might be one of them.
He said, well, if that's what's going on, what do I do?
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，如果真是这样，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: I said, well, you do this as well as you can.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，那就尽可能好地过好这段生活。

sentences.en: So we had a long conversation about that.
sentences.zh: 于是我们对此进行了长时间的交谈。

sentences.en: It must have been very difficult for you to say what you said to him, Dave, but also very difficult for him to listen to it.
sentences.zh: 对你说出你对他说的话一定很难，戴夫，但对他来说听进去也很不容易。

sentences.en: This is not the kind of thing that a friend is supposed to tell you.
sentences.zh: 这不是朋友应该对你说的那种话。

sentences.en: Well, this is where we make the distinction between nice and loving.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我们区分“友善”与“爱”的地方。

sentences.en: You know, are you trying to be nice to somebody or trying to love them?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你是试图对别人友善，还是试图去爱他们？

sentences.en: And sometimes that love, I don't mean tough love, and you have to beat them up.
sentences.zh: 有时那种爱——我不是指严厉的爱，你必须痛打他们。

sentences.en: I wasn't trying to be unkind.
sentences.zh: 我并不是想表现得不友好。

sentences.en: But if it's true that he's going to die of a stroke, which he did about four strokes later,
sentences.zh: 但如果他真的会死于中风——他在大约四次中风后确实如此——

sentences.en: then either he's going to do that and be blindsided by it and terrified at the moment of death
sentences.zh: 那么要么他会这样死去，并在临终时感到措手不及和恐惧，

sentences.en: and leave his family in some despair about his final days,
sentences.zh: 并在他生命的最后几天让他的家人感到绝望，

sentences.en: or he's got a little more time to do this well.
sentences.zh: 或者他还有多一点时间把这件事情做好。

sentences.en: So what's the kindest thing I can do?
sentences.zh: 所以我能做的最善良的事情是什么？

sentences.en: The kindest thing I can do is give him a shot at the invitation
sentences.zh: 我能做的最善良的事情就是给他一个机会，去邀请他

sentences.en: to actually find the meaning and the joy that is available.
sentences.zh: 真正找到那份本可获得的意义和快乐。

sentences.en: I'm not in charge of his fixing his brain, but I might be able to give him an invitation
sentences.zh: 我并不负责修复他的大脑，但我或许可以向他发出邀请，

sentences.en: to a little more life-giving experience than he's currently having.
sentences.zh: 去体验比他目前更多的生命活力。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how Gary took your advice and what he did with it.
sentences.zh: 我想知道加里是如何接受你的建议的，他又是如何处理的。

sentences.en: Well, we had that conversation, and he received it reasonably well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们进行了那次谈话，他相当不错地接受了。

sentences.en: But, I mean, it was really hard, and it was pretty quiet.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，这真的很艰难，而且非常安静。

sentences.en: And his wife, Kathy, was in the kitchen and over here, you know,
sentences.zh: 他的妻子凯茜在厨房里，在这一边，你知道，

sentences.en: and kind of gave us some space.
sentences.zh: 给我们留出了一些空间。

sentences.en: And I didn't really know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我当时并不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I bumped into his wife in the supermarket about three weeks later,
sentences.zh: 大约三周后，我在超市偶遇了他的妻子，

sentences.en: and she walks up to me.
She goes, what was it you said to Gary?
sentences.zh: 她说，你对加里说了什么？

sentences.en: And I thought, oh, man, this is going to go badly.
And I said, well, this is what I said.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，好吧，我是这样说的。

sentences.en: And she said, well, it made all the difference in the world.
sentences.zh: 她说，这可真是起到了至关重要的作用。

sentences.en: So, phew, you know, dodged that bullet.
sentences.zh: 所以，呼，你知道，总算有惊无险。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's kind of hitting me again.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，这种感觉又涌上心头了。

sentences.en: This life stuff, you know, it's pretty serious,
sentences.zh: 生活中的这些事，你知道，挺沉重的，

sentences.en: but it's the best thing we've got.
sentences.zh: 但这也是我们拥有的最好的东西。

sentences.en: And so the invitation is, would you like to participate?
sentences.zh: 所以我们的邀请是，你愿意参与进来吗？

sentences.en: When we come back, why the most important thing
sentences.zh: 节目稍后回来，为什么最重要的事情

sentences.en: might not be figuring out where you want to go,
sentences.zh: 可能不是去想你想去哪里，

sentences.en: but accepting where it is you are.
sentences.zh: 而是接受你当下所在的地方。
你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: At Stanford University, Dave Evans studies a concept called design thinking.
sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，戴夫·埃文斯研究一个叫作设计思维的概念。

sentences.en: He says that the same principles that engineers and innovators use to solve complex problems
sentences.zh: 他说，工程师和创新者用来解决复杂问题的那些原则

sentences.en: can also be applied to designing our lives,
